question: The difference (in Rs., to the nearest integer) between the simple interest and the compound interest on Rs. 3,660 for one and a half years at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly, is:
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹3,660

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% p.a.

Time (T) = 1.5 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (S.I.) = dfrac{P times R times T}{100}

Compound Interest (C.I.) = P(1+dfrac{r}{100})^n - P

**Calculation:**

S.I. = dfrac{3660 times 10 times 1.5}{100}

⇒ S.I. = ₹549

For C.I. compounded half-yearly:

Rate per half year = dfrac{10}{2} = 5\%, Number of half-years (n) = 1.5 times 2 = 3

C.I. = 3660 (1+dfrac{5}{100})³ - 3660

⇒ C.I. = 3660 times dfrac{21}{20} times dfrac{21}{20} times dfrac{21}{20} - 3660

⇒ C.I. = ₹576.9 approx 577

Required Difference = 577 - 549 = ₹28

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28.**
